HOLD: a real, identified macro/political catalyst today, not a company-specific break -- shares fell sharply (~9-12% intraday per multiple sources) after Tuesday's Democratic sweep of Congress revived fears that Washington could slow US data-center construction (Texas's governor-elect campaigned on a data-center moratorium); GE Vernova (-8%), Vistra (-10%) and Constellation (-6%) fell the same day on the identical theme, confirming this is sector-wide beta, not VRT-specific news. No earnings miss, guidance cut, or litigation escalation found; organic orders more than doubled per 11/3's confirmed fundamentals (revenue growth +61.2% YoY, earnings growth +91.2% YoY, fundamentals API down again today so no fresher figures), and Congress has no direct say over backlog already booked. Several commentators call the selloff overdone. Stop-loss flag deepened sharply to -36.4% (from -27.0% on 11/3) -- a fresh macro-beta-driven crossing (same pattern as the 9/16/26 review), watching for any follow-through into actual policy action rather than treating the headline-driven drop alone as thesis-breaking. Position ~7.4%.

But shares still sold off hard (~9-14% intraday per several sources) because Q4 guidance of $1.19-1.20B implies roughly flat-to-down sequential revenue, which multiple outlets tie to Datadog's largest (undisclosed) customer cutting usage down to its minimum commitment -- a concrete, real materialization of customer-concentration risk, not just a beat-and-fade. This is a genuine new data point worth tracking (is it one customer's idiosyncratic pullback or a broader AI-spend normalization?), but a 35%-YoY-growing, FY-guidance-raising business missing on one forward quarter from one customer isn't thesis-breaking on its own.
